subject: see effect of covariate vs effect of treatment (or main factor)

messages.author: 88f4d2b71dfaedcd
messages.subject: see effect of covariate vs effect of treatment (or main factor)
parts:
Dear all,

I have run Methylkit to compare the metylation levels between 2 groups, so I use a binomial test afterwards. I have introduced a covariate, as my data might have internal structure (samples come from different bee colonies), but they might have not cause I am working with pure genetic lines, so maybe the colony effect here is not relevant. I could not find a way yet to see to what extent (statistically speaking) is worth including my covariate, and how much of the methylation differences is this factor explaining. Could somebody help me there, please?

Kind regards,

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] see effect of covariate vs effect of treatment (or main factor)
parts:
you can try to run the test with treatment only and treatment+covariate. If the covariate do not have a significant effect (does not explain the variation in methylation levels) you will have the same number of differentially methylated CpGs. 

Best,
Altuna
